Indian Statistical Institute
Admission 2026-2027
Selection Policy and Business Rules
for Admission 2026–2027 (B SDS)
The Indian Statistical Institute offers several academic programmes.
Details about these pro-
grammes, along with the category-wise intake capacity, can be found on the online portal:
https://admission.isical.ac.in/.
The business rules stated herein will be followed in the academic year 2026–27 for allocating seats
for the B SDS programme.
Admission to the B SDS programme will be based on performance in one or more of the following
national examinations:
• JEE Main 2026
• CUET (UG) 2026 (Mathematics as well as English)
• JEE Main 2025
• CUET (UG) 2025 (Mathematics as well as English)
At the time of application, candidates must submit application numbers for one or more of these
national examinations.
All applicants for whom at least one score is available by a speciﬁed
deadline (30 June, 2026) and at least one of the available scores exceeds a minimum cutoff will be

national examinations.
All applicants for whom at least one score is available by a speciﬁed
deadline (30 June, 2026) and at least one of the available scores exceeds a minimum cutoff will be
placed on one or more Merit Lists as per their category (see Section 3).
Seats are allocated to candidates considering the following factors:
(i) The category [GEN, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, PwBD, EWS] of the candidate.
(ii) The position of the candidate in Merit List(s).
(iii) Availability of seats at different centres of the Institute.
(iv) Other business rules as mentioned in this document.
1
Ranking of Candidates
The position of an applicant in the Merit List(s) is based on a composite score Q derived from their
performance in the national examinations mentioned above for which the candidate has speciﬁed
an application number, and whose scores are available by the speciﬁed deadline. For two or more
applicants with the same composite score Q, their relative position will be determined according

an application number, and whose scores are available by the speciﬁed deadline. For two or more
applicants with the same composite score Q, their relative position will be determined according
to tie-breaking criteria T1 and T2.

1. The composite score Q is the maximum of the available percentiles for Mathematics in JEE
Main 2026, CUET (UG) 2026, JEE Main 2025, and CUET (UG) 2025. If none of these per-
centiles are available, then Q is invalid.
2. The ﬁrst tie-breaker T1 is calculated as follows:
• If Q equals the candidate’s JEE 2026 Mathematics percentile, then T1 is their JEE 2026
total percentile.
• Otherwise, if Q equals the candidate’s CUET (UG) 2026 Mathematics percentile, then
T1 is their CUET (UG) 2026 English percentile.
• Otherwise, if Q equals the candidate’s JEE 2025 Mathematics percentile, then T1 is their
JEE 2025 total percentile.
• Otherwise, if Q equals the candidate’s CUET (UG) 2025 Mathematics percentile, then
T1 is their CUET (UG) 2025 English percentile.
3. The second tie-breaker T2 is the age of the candidate in days as on May 31, 2026.
4. Candidates are placed in the Merit List according to Q (candidates with higher values of Q

3. The second tie-breaker T2 is the age of the candidate in days as on May 31, 2026.
4. Candidates are placed in the Merit List according to Q (candidates with higher values of Q
will be placed higher on the Merit List).
5. For two or more applicants with the same composite score Q, their relative position in the
Merit List will be determined according to T1 (candidates with higher values of T1 will be
placed higher on the Merit List).
6. For two or more applicants with the same values of Q as well as T1, their relative position in
the Merit List will be determined according to T2 (candidates with lower values of T2 will be
placed higher on the Merit List).
2
Categories of Candidates
For the purpose of admission, all candidates with a valid composite score Q will be partitioned into
different categories based on (birth) categories, presence or absence of disability, and nationality.
On the basis of such a partition, each candidate is assigned a category tag as given below.
2

GEN:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who do NOT belong to EWS, OBC-NCL,
SC or ST category (or who fail to produce valid EWS, OBC-NCL, SC or ST certiﬁ-
cate) and are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities.
GEN-PwBD:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who do NOT belong to EWS, OBC-NCL,
SC or ST category (or who fail to produce valid EWS, OBC-NCL, SC or ST cer-
tiﬁcate) and are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce a
valid PwBD certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.
GEN-EWS:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals of General category belonging to Eco-
nomically Weaker Section (EWS) as deﬁned in Order No.36039/1/2019-Estt (Res),
Government of India, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, De-
partment of Personnel & Training, and are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabil-
ities. Candidate must produce a valid GEN-EWS certiﬁcate to be assigned this
tag.
GEN-EWS-PwBD:

partment of Personnel & Training, and are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabil-
ities. Candidate must produce a valid GEN-EWS certiﬁcate to be assigned this
tag.
GEN-EWS-PwBD:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals of GEN-PwBD category belonging to Eco-
nomically Weaker Section (EWS) as deﬁned in Order No.36039/1/2019-Estt (Res),
Government of India, Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pensions, De-
partment of Personnel & Training, and are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities.
Candidates must produce valid GEN-EWS and PwBD certiﬁcates to be assigned
this tag. Thus, candidates belonging to the economically-weaker sections of the
general category are divided into two mutually exclusive categories and are as-
signed either one of the tags GEN-EWS or GEN-EWS-PwBD.
OBC-NCL:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to the Non-Creamy Layer
of Other Backward Classes and are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities.

OBC-NCL:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to the Non-Creamy Layer
of Other Backward Classes and are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities.
Candidates must produce a valid OBC-NCL certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.
The backward class must be in the Central List of OBCs.
OBC-NCL-PwBD:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to the Non-Creamy Layer of
Other Backward Classes and are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates
must produce valid OBC-NCL and PwBD certiﬁcates to be assigned this tag. The
backward class must be in the Central List of OBCs. Thus, candidates belonging to
the Non-Creamy Layer of Other Backward Classes are divided into two mutually
exclusive categories and are assigned either one of the tags OBC-NCL or OBC-
NCL-PwBD.
SC:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to Scheduled Castes and are
NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce a valid SC
certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.
SC-PwBD:

NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce a valid SC
certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.
SC-PwBD:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to Scheduled Castes and
are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce valid SC and
PwBD certiﬁcates to be assigned this tag. Thus, candidates belonging to the sched-
uled castes are divided into two mutually exclusive categories and are assigned
either one of the tags SC or SC-PwBD.

ST:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to Scheduled Tribes and
are NOT Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce a
valid ST certiﬁcate to be assigned this tag.
ST-PwBD:
This tag is assigned to Indian nationals who belong to Scheduled Tribes and
are Persons with Benchmark Disabilities. Candidates must produce valid ST
and PwBD certiﬁcates to be assigned this tag. Thus, candidates belonging to
the scheduled tribes are divided into two mutually exclusive categories and
are assigned either one of the tags ST or ST-PwBD.
3
Merit lists
The following Merit Lists will be prepared for admission to the B SDS programme, according to
the procedure described in Section 1. Only those candidates will be placed on the merit list whose
composite score Q exceeds 85 (80 for OBC-NCL and 75 for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates).
(i) GEN merit list : It includes all candidates who have obtained a valid composite score Q, and

composite score Q exceeds 85 (80 for OBC-NCL and 75 for SC, ST, and PwBD candidates).
(i) GEN merit list : It includes all candidates who have obtained a valid composite score Q, and
Q exceeds 85.
(ii) GEN-EWS merit list : It includes candidates who are assigned the tag GEN-EWS or GEN-
EWS-PwBD, have obtained a valid composite score Q, and Q exceeds 85.
(iii) OBC-NCL merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag OBC-NCL or OBC-
NCL-PwBD, have obtained a valid composite score Q, and Q exceeds 80.
(iv) SC merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag SC or SC-PwBD, have obtained
a valid composite score Q, and Q exceeds 75.
(v) ST merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag ST or ST-PwBD, have obtained
a valid composite score Q, and Q exceeds 75.
(vi) GEN-PwBD merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag GEN-PwBD, GEN-
EWS-PwBD, OBC-NCL-PwBD, SC-PwBD, or ST-PwBD, have obtained a valid composite
score Q, and Q exceeds 75.

(vi) GEN-PwBD merit list: It includes candidates who are assigned the tag GEN-PwBD, GEN-
EWS-PwBD, OBC-NCL-PwBD, SC-PwBD, or ST-PwBD, have obtained a valid composite
score Q, and Q exceeds 75.
4

GEN-EWS, OBC-NCL, SC, ST, GEN-PwBD. The category tags of candidates who are eligible for

4. Seats in different centres are allocated according to the following rules.
• Step 1: Candidates admitted through the general merit list are tentatively allocated to the

• Step 2: Allocation of centre for the reserved category candidates are ﬁnalized according to

5. Rules for de-reservation of seats are as follows.
(a) If the number of seats in GEN-PwBD category in any particular round of seat allocation
is greater than the number of candidates in the GEN-PwBD list then the difference will be
de-reserved and treated as GEN category seats.
(b) If the number of seats in OBC-NCL category in any particular round of seat allocation

de-reserved and treated as GEN category seats.
(b) If the number of seats in OBC-NCL category in any particular round of seat allocation
is greater than the number of candidates in the OBC-NCL list then the difference will be
de-reserved as GEN category seats.

Admission Procedure
6.1
Provisional Allocation of Seats
1. From the merit list(s) and the sequencing order speciﬁed in Section 5, provisional allocation
of seats will be made to eligible candidates. In each round, each candidate on the merit

1. From the merit list(s) and the sequencing order speciﬁed in Section 5, provisional allocation
of seats will be made to eligible candidates. In each round, each candidate on the merit
list(s) will either be allocated a provisional seat or put on the wait list. If a candidate accepts
the offer of a provisional seat in a location other than their ﬁrst preference, they will still be
considered for upgradation of their allocated location in subsequent rounds.
2. Candidates will be given a time window in each round to ﬁll-in their options:
(a) If a candidate is offered a provisional seat, then the candidate has the option of accepting
or declining the provisional seat.
(b) While accepting the provisional seat offer, a candidate will be required to pay a ‘Seat
Acceptance Deposit’.
(c) If a candidate is offered a position on the wait list, then the candidate has the option of
accepting or declining to remain on the wait list.

Acceptance Deposit’.
(c) If a candidate is offered a position on the wait list, then the candidate has the option of
accepting or declining to remain on the wait list.
(d) Filling-in of options on the online portal for waitlisted candidates is free of cost, i.e.,
candidates who are waitlisted are NOT required to pay any deposit while accepting the
offer.
(e) Any candidate on the merit list(s) who does not ﬁll in the option within the given time
limit will be assumed to have declined the respective option.
(f) In the ﬁrst round of seat allocation, while accepting the provisional seat or accepting a
wait list offer, a candidate will have to complete registration formalities. In subsequent
rounds, if the offer changes, candidates will have to accept/decline the option again.
(g) A candidate who has declined a provisional seat offer or wait list offer at any round is
NOT considered for the rest of the admission process.

(g) A candidate who has declined a provisional seat offer or wait list offer at any round is
NOT considered for the rest of the admission process.
(h) Candidates will NOT be able to change their options once submitted in any speciﬁc
round.

6.2
Provisional Seats to Conﬁrmation of Admission
1. A candidate who accepts a provisional seat offer will be able to download a Provisional
Seat Allocation Letter which will specify date of reporting, reporting centre and ﬁnancial fee
details.
2. Candidates who have accepted a provisional seat should report at a Reporting Center for
document veriﬁcation on the speciﬁed date.
3. If a candidate accepts a provisional seat then the candidate’s admission will be conﬁrmed
by the Reporting Centre after veriﬁcation of the original documents and ensuring that the
candidate meets all the eligibility norms. Failure to report in person for seat acceptance will
be considered as if the candidate has declined the provisional seat offer.
7
Miscellaneous
1. Mismatches between the personal information submitted in the Application Portal and the
personal information associated with application numbers for JEE Main and/or CUET (UG)

7
Miscellaneous
1. Mismatches between the personal information submitted in the Application Portal and the
personal information associated with application numbers for JEE Main and/or CUET (UG)
may lead to the cancellation of an application.
2. The deadline for availability of scores of national examinations considered for calculation of
the composite score Q may be extended. Any such change will be notiﬁed on the website
https://admission.isical.ac.in/.
The decisions taken in this regard shall be ﬁnal and binding.
3. Delays or disruptions in service due to breakdown of admission portals/computer servers
(due to reasons beyond control) shall be rectiﬁed as early as possible and notiﬁed on the
website
https://admission.isical.ac.in/.
The decisions taken in this regard shall be ﬁnal and binding.
4. The admission process for a programme will close when all scheduled physical admissions
and spot admissions (if any) are completed.
